title: Cloudflare Develops Public Certificate Authority for Post-Quantum Web Security
gist: Cloudflare's Chrome experiment with Merkle Tree Certificates showed 9% faster median performance using classical signatures, and Cloudflare is now building a public CA aiming for Chrome's quantum-resistant Root Store in early 2027, subject to evaluation.

insights.claim: Cloudflare reported 9% faster median performance for Merkle Tree Certificates versus traditional certificate chains in a Chrome experiment.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Evidence that post-quantum-ready PKI designs need not cost web performance.
insights.locator: Cloudflare has tested Merkle Tree Certificates

insights.claim: Cloudflare attributed most of the measured speedup to eliminating intermediate certificates, and the experiment used classical rather than post-quantum signatures, so it does not directly measure post-quantum overhead.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Caveat: the headline gain is not a post-quantum result.
insights.locator: Cloudflare attributed most of the measured improvement

insights.claim: The experiment served billions of MTCs to 50% of Chrome Beta 146 for selected domains on Cloudflare's free plan before being wound down in August 2026.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Shows testing at meaningful production scale.
insights.locator: The experiment served billions of MTCs

themes.theme: Post-quantum scaling pressure on Web PKI

insights.claim: Post-quantum signatures can be approximately 40 times larger than classical signatures, increasing bandwidth and storage requirements for Web PKI.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Size inflation is the core cost driver pushing redesign of certificate infrastructure.

insights.claim: Cloudflare's CEO frames upgrading web security before quantum computers can break it as one of the biggest coordination challenges in Internet history.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Signals multi-party coordination, not technology, is the bottleneck for migration.
insights.quote: Upgrading the web's security before quantum computers can break it is one of the biggest coordination challenges in the history of the Internet.

insights.claim: MTCs replace per-certificate signing with a CA recording certificate data in an append-only Merkle tree and signing a checkpoint, so clients verify inclusion via compact proofs.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Combines issuance with transparency logging, reducing handshake data.
insights.locator: MTCs combine certificate issuance with transparency logging

insights.claim: In the common case a landmark-relative TLS handshake transmits one public key, one signature, and an inclusion proof smaller than 1 KB, with servers keeping a standalone MTC as fallback for clients lacking the landmark.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Fallback requirement adds complexity during rollout.
insights.locator: Landmark relative certificates further reduce TLS handshake data

insights.claim: An independent mirroring cosigner stores updated tree states, helping detect inconsistent log views and preserving issuance records if the original log becomes unavailable.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Trust is distributed across cosigners rather than a single CA.

insights.claim: Cloudflare is developing a public CA supporting MTC issuance, targeting inclusion in Chrome's quantum-resistant Root Store in early 2027, subject to evaluation.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Browser acceptance gates adoption and Cloudflare's positioning in post-quantum PKI.

insights.claim: Cloudflare identifies independent monitoring at production volume, a diverse ecosystem of CAs and cosigners, and browser support as remaining requirements for broader deployment.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili

insights.claim: An SSL.com specialist argued that with short validity and trust anchored in a tree head, the OCSP and CRL revocation playbook becomes a question of how quickly a certificate can stop being included.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Revocation and incident handling remain open operational questions.
insights.quote: a lot of the old OCSP and CRL playbook becomes a question of how quickly you can stop including a certificate
